recentItems.title: Joe Bonamassa on 75 Years of the Fender Telecaster
recentItems.description:
“I always say Leo Fender got it right the first time a lot of times,” says Joe Bonamassa, “and this is the electric guitar that basically changed the world of rock and roll after it was introduced 75 years ago.”
 
Celebrate the “Diamond Jubilee” of the Fender Telecaster as Bonamassa—one of the world’s premier (and enthusiastic) vintage guitar collectors—talks about the birth, evolution and sonic majesty of Leo Fender’s iconic solidbody.
 
In this video:
• Learn Leo Fender’s original intention for the Telecaster
• Meet Bonamassa’s Los Angeles “session” Tele
• Discover some Telecaster virtuosos
• Hear why Joe Bonamassa prefers vintage guitars with personality—even if they "break."
 
What's your favorite Telecaster model, player or story? Share it in the comments.

recentItems.title: Eric Clapton Reacts to His New Martin Guitars | Crossroads 2026
recentItems.description:
Eric Clapton gets a first look at the Martin guitars created for his signature Crossroads 2026 Collection from long-time friend Michael Doyle. In this exclusive Guitar Center video, Clapton and Doyle discuss the legendary guitarist’s passion for acoustic guitars and playing acoustic, while looking at the Guitar Center-exclusive Martin 000-42 EC and Martin 000-13 EC (Guitar Center-exclusive through 1/27/27). The conversation also explores the acoustic blues artists whose recordings inspired Clapton to pick up the guitar.   
 
“I started on the acoustic,” says Clapton. “And when I practice, I practice on an acoustic. It makes you play a certain way. I always revert to what I heard as a kid that made me want to play, and that was acoustic blues.”
 
In this video:
• Discover why Clapton didn’t want to release his 1992 MTV Unplugged album
• Find out Clapton’s favorite body shape for acoustic guitars
• Learn what shocked Clapton about hearing Muddy Waters perform in England in 1958
• Hear what Clapton considers his “main cause”

recentItems.title: Eric Clapton Checks out the NEW Fender "Blind Faith" Tele | Crossroads 2026
recentItems.description:
Michael Doyle shows his long-time friend Eric Clapton the new reissue inspired by the vintage Fender Telecaster Clapton played in Blind Faith. Part of the Eric Clapton Crossroads 2026 Collection, the Guitar Center exclusive Blind Faith Telecaster was built at Fender’s Corona, California factory (the 2019 reissue was a Custom Shop model) and joins other Clapton signatures, such as the Martin Custom Shop 000-42 acoustic, Martin 000-13E acoustic electric and Ernie Ball 2026 Crossroads electric guitar strings.
 
“That was the thing about Fenders—the bits of parts,” says Clapton. “Good fun. Like Lego [blocks], you could make your own guitar. Which I did with my Blackie Stratocaster. It was made from four different vintage Strats.”
 
In this video:
• Discover the “special” neck-pickup tone of Clapton’s original Blind Faith Tele
• Learn one of the reasons why Clapton “moved on” from the Telecaster to the Stratocaster
• Hear Clapton reminiscing whether the “Presence of the Lord” riff was played on a Tele or not
• Figure out the guitar part that some players used but many removed entirely

recentItems.title: WATCH the Full Guitar Center Drum-Off 2026 Competition
recentItems.description:
Join the energy of a capacity crowd at Guitar Center Drum-Off 2026 for “fills and thrills” as six finalists take the stage to unleash six explosive drum solos. Watch as hosts Bill Burr (comedian/drummer) and Stephen Perkins (Jane’s Addiction, Porno for Pyros, Hellride) set the stage for these “drum legends in the making” and introduce the house band of Rob Trujillo (Metallica), Dave Kushner (Velvet Revolver) and Dean Pleasants (Suicidal Tendencies).
 
For its 2026 return, Guitar Center’s Drum-Off changed up the format. Rather than have each drummer blast off into a five-minute drum solo, each finalist started off performing a one-minute jam with the house band—choosing from a selection of instrumental songs that were written specifically for the competition. Then, Jonathan Fortson, Michael-Andrew Cornish, Christopher “CJ” Darden, Mitch Gorman, Caleb Robinson and Jake Ward each launched into their solo performances.
 
“It has been ten years since we’ve been here,” said Perkins in his opening remarks. “Tonight is going to be incredible. We have great performances, celebrity judges and contestants that are going to blow our minds.”
 
“I have to be honest,” added Burr. “The level you kids are playing at is beyond everything I watch [to learn drums]. You guys are unbelievable and very inspiring.”
 
Guitar Center’s Drum-Off 2026 was sponsored by DW and Zildjian, and held August 20, at the iconic Fonda Theatre in Los Angeles. 

Microphones for Competition Kits provided by Sennheiser.

recentItems.title: Jimmy Eat World: “We share a desire to do what’s right for the music” | Inside the Noise (S3, E6)
recentItems.description:
Taking a break from their Vans Warped Tour set, Jimmy Eat World—lead guitarist/vocalist Jim Adkins, rhythm guitarist/vocalist Tom Linton, bassist Rick Burch and drummer Zach Lind—joins Guitar Center CEO Gabe Dalporto backstage to discuss the 25th anniversary of the alternative-rock band’s platinum-selling Bleed American album, collaborating on songwriting and how the business of making music has changed.
 
“One thing we appreciate more now is cherishing moments as they happen and acknowledging the good things that come your way,” says Burch.
 
“Yeah, when you’re in your early 20s, the idea of savoring experiences—those muscles aren’t fully formed yet,” adds Adkins. “But every little win is going to be so much richer if you can focus and be present as it’s happening.”
 
In this episode:
• Discover how Jimmy Eat World has stayed together and creatively productive for more than three decades
• Hear what Jimmy Eat World loves about playing the Vans Warped Tour
• Learn how making money as a musician has changed
• Find out why playing Saturday Night Live was so nerve-wracking
 
SUBSCRIBE for more conversations with artists, producers, industry leaders and innovators.

recentItems.title: Gibson's Mat Koehler on Why Guitar Endures | Inside the Noise (Season 3 Highlights)
recentItems.description:
Gibson Vice President of Product Mat Koehler hangs out with Guitar Center CEO Gabe Dalporto to discuss the undeniable attraction of vintage guitars, the company’s Murphy Lab recreations of nearly unobtainable vintage classics, and how Epiphone allows the team to play around with new and more contemporary franchises.
 
Koehler also dives into how the Gibson Custom Shop and Murphy Lab continue closing the gap between vintage originals and modern recreations, and explains how Gibson balances its historic legacy with the needs of today’s players and artists.

recentItems.title: WATCH Guitar Center's 2026 Drum-Off Winner - Jonathan Fortson
recentItems.description:
Experience the thrilling drum solo, mammoth grooves and unforgettable charisma, as Jonathan Fortson wins the title of Guitar Center Drum-Off 2026 Champion.
 
Fortson’s performance opened as a funky and boisterous jam with bassist Rob Trujillo (Metallica) and guitarists Dave Kushner (Velvet Revolver) and Dean Pleasants (Suicidal Tendencies). After the players walked off, leaving Fortson in the spotlight, he broke things down with some gentle sticks-on-rims parts before switching to mallets for flurries of dynamic rhythmic swings. The percussive ebbs and flows continued when Fortson grabbed his drumsticks again, taking the audience through a series of explosive tom fills, driving snare and ride cymbal patterns, and some slick “whirling arms” punctuations.
 
Fortson's astounding drum solo was the crescendo for an evening that saw the legendary competition return after a decade-long hiatus. To take the title, he had to wow a group of iconic drummers (judges included Tré Cool, Adrian Young, John Stamos, Alex González and Brad Wilk) and overcome some astounding drum solos from five formidable finalists (Mitch Gorman, Caleb Robinson, Christopher "CJ" Darden, Michael-Andrew Cornish and Jake Ward).
 
The Guitar Center Drum-Off 2026 was held at The Fonda Theatre in Los Angeles and was hosted by comedian/drummer Bill Burr and Stephen Perkins (Jane’s Addiction, Porno for Pyros, Hellride).
